description:
A MEASURED RUNTIME REGRESSION, not a codegen-shape nit. Found by fz-kdt.93,
confirmed and quantified by the adversarial review of that commit.

## The number

scratchpad/deep_split.fz -- Enum.split_while + Enum.split_with over a
30,000-element list, AOT (`fz2 build`), compile floor identical between
revisions:

    reviewer     base d5d45a074   48.3s / 48.5s
                 fz-kdt.93        58.2s / 59.0s      ~ +20%

    builder      base d5d45a074   44.45s / 43.82s
                 fz-kdt.93        58.17s / 55.38s
                 + closure fix    55.80s / 55.52s    ~ +26%

Two machines, same direction and magnitude. The blocker fix that landed with
fz-kdt.93 (the grounded closure-call cut) does not move it: the cost is the
return-contract disagreement below, not the closure edge.

## The shape it takes in the artifact

On 00420_enum_take_drop_split, 13 recursive `direct_call ... -> return` edges
turned `return_flow=tail` into `return_flow=continue(shape{...})`, and
`fz.codegen.define_function` rose 1087 -> 1100. enum_predicate_search moves the
other way (5 continue -> tail, 2 tail -> continue; 658 -> 655 functions);
fz_f98_range_map_converges does not move. No PINNED budget moved -- the matrix
is green and none of the three lens fixtures carries a budget assertion -- so
nothing caught this except the runtime measurement.

## Mechanism

At a cut position the layout comes from `cut_transport_layout`
(jobs/transport.rs). An `ExecutableReturn` with several origins usually still
has READABLE evidence beside the cut arm, and that evidence carries its type,
so it keeps the evidence form -- e.g. `lane({list(int), :false | :true})`. The
matching `ReturnPayload` for the same call has only the ONE cut origin, so it
has no evidence and falls back to the type contract, which decomposes an exact
tuple type -- `shape{lane(list), lane(:false | :true)}`. The artifact's
`CallReturnFlow` (jobs/artifact.rs, `ControlDestination::Return` arm) requires
source == caller_return == payload for a `Tail` and emits `Continue`
otherwise, so the caller re-materializes: it builds the pair unboxed at the
callee and boxes it again on the way out, once per recursive call, on the hot
edge of a 30,000-iteration loop.

Base did not have this because the knot group stamped ONE layout on every
member, forcing agreement -- the very lottery fz-kdt.93 removed. The agreement
was real; only the way it was reached was a race.

## Direction

The two positions are two views of ONE calling convention and must derive one
contract. Candidates, both cheap to measure:

  (a) the payload prefers its callee's published return layout when that
      layout carries the payload's type -- the callee return is already a fact
      edge in this cone, so no new dependency;
  (b) an `ExecutableReturn` inside a cut cycle takes the same type contract its
      payload takes, so neither side invents alone.

Gate the choice on tools/canon-gate.sh d5d45a074 over the three lens fixtures:
the target is 0 net tail -> continue with the 44 gained decomposed forms kept,
and deep_split.fz back to the base 44s band.
title: Cut positions and their callers invent different return contracts: a ~25% runtime regression on split_while/split_with
